title: The Big Nothing — A Code-Driven Short

scenes.title: The Big Nothing
scenes.subtitle: A short film, written in JSON
scenes.voiceover: This is a short film. It was written in JSON, rendered by code, and directed by a model that has never seen a sunrise.

scenes.heading: Three minutes. Four acts. One pipeline.
scenes.voiceover: Three minutes. Four acts. One pipeline. Each act is a stage where a human idea is transformed, by a different machine, into something a little closer to a film.

scenes.heading: It begins with a sentence
bullets: Make me a three minute movie
scenes.voiceover: Every film starts with someone wanting something. A sentence. A request. Make me a three minute movie. About what? About this — about the asking itself. Okay.

scenes.heading: What the prompt actually is
scenes.voiceover: A prompt is a wish, compressed. It's ambiguity deferred to the machine. It's authorship distributed across whoever wrote the model, whoever wrote the tool, whoever wrote the request. It is trust, extended on credit.

scenes.heading: The script writes itself
scenes.voiceover: The script writes itself, in a way. Scenes become objects. Beats become durations. The voiceover becomes a string. The string becomes a file on disk, waiting to be read.

scenes.heading: The model chooses for you
scenes.voiceover: The model chooses things you used to choose yourself. The pacing. The pauses. How many words fit in a second. Where the silence goes. You can argue with it. Often you don't.

scenes.heading: Synthetic, but not impersonal
scenes.voiceover: The voice is synthetic, but it is not impersonal. It was trained on thousands of human readers. It was tuned by a loss function nobody can fully describe. It is never tired, never thirsty. It is also never quite present.

scenes.heading: The uncanny valley question
scenes.voiceover: Is it close enough to a real voice? Is close enough enough? Or is the closeness itself the thing that bothers us? People keep watching, either way.

scenes.heading: Frames are math
scenes.voiceover: Frames are math. Nineteen twenty by ten eighty. Thirty frames a second. Five thousand four hundred frames in this film. Each one a small decision, made too fast for anyone to feel.

scenes.heading: What you are watching
bullets: A plan that emerged from a sentence
A sentence that began as a thought
A thought that wanted to become a thing
scenes.voiceover: What you are watching is a program executing a plan. The plan emerged from a sentence. The sentence began as a thought. The thought wanted to become a thing in the world.

scenes.title: Made by asking
scenes.subtitle: Render finished. The big nothing, briefly, became something.
scenes.voiceover: Made by asking. The render is finished. The big nothing, briefly, became something.
